verdict.rationale: Runloop's own docs describe Devboxes as "isolated Linux sandbox environments" and "secure sandboxed execution environments", so it does claim isolation between sandboxes and the user's systems. However, nothing in the evidence documents the boundary type (microVM, VM, hypervisor or equivalent), so the 'hard' part of the story is unproven. Egress network policies are a related control, not proof of the isolation boundary itself. Missing for 10: documented isolation mechanism (microVM/hypervisor or equivalent), technical description of the boundary between tenants and the host, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can rely on a documented hard isolation boundary (microVM or equivalent) between sandboxes and my systems

citations.quote: Runloop is the best platform for running isolated Linux sandbox environments (Devboxes) for AI coding agent
Runloop provides secure sandboxed execution environments called Devboxes.
